problems.title: 68% Cart Abandonment — $18K+/Month Left in Carts
problems.description: Nearly 7 out of 10 shoppers add needlepoint kits to their cart and leave without buying. For a niche ecommerce store with an $85 average order value, every abandoned cart is a warm buyer who got distracted, had a question about skill level, or wasn't sure which thread weight to pick. Without an automated recovery sequence, those buyers are gone — many to mass retailers or Etsy sellers.
problems.impact: At 320 orders/month with 68% abandonment, ~680 carts are abandoned monthly. Recovering just 10% at $85 AOV = $5,780/month in recovered revenue.
problems.evidence: Baymard Institute: average ecommerce cart abandonment rate is 70.19%. Niche craft stores with high-consideration products often exceed this. Art Needlepoint's product requires skill-level matching — a key friction point.

problems.title: Only 47 Google Reviews — Trust Gap in a Visual Product Category
problems.description: Needlepoint is a visual, tactile craft. Buyers need to trust that the canvas quality, thread colors, and design details match the photos. With only 47 Google reviews, Art Needlepoint is under-indexed on trust signals compared to competitors. The real gold is in customer photos of finished projects — the 'Strut Your Stitches' gallery exists but isn't systematically fed. Happy customers who spent 40–200 hours stitching a project have deep emotional connection to share — but nobody asks at the right moment.
problems.impact: Thin review profile reduces conversion rate by an estimated 15–25%. Each 0.1 star improvement in rating drives 2–5% more clicks from Google Shopping.
problems.evidence: PowerReviews: 97% of consumers read reviews before buying. For craft products, photo reviews convert 3x better than text-only reviews.

problems.title: No Sentiment Filter — Unhappy Customers Get Review Links, Happy Ones Don't
problems.description: Currently, there's no system to gauge customer satisfaction before asking for a review. A customer who received the wrong thread color or found the canvas smaller than expected gets the same (or no) review request as a delighted customer who just finished a 6-month stocking project. Without sentiment analysis, you risk amplifying negative experiences publicly while missing the window to capture glowing transformational reviews from your happiest customers.
problems.impact: One 1-star review can reduce conversion by 10–15% in a niche market. Pre-screening sentiment prevents public damage and routes unhappy customers to support instead.
problems.evidence: Harvard Business School: a one-star increase in Yelp rating leads to 5–9% revenue increase. Negative reviews in craft/hobby spaces are disproportionately damaging because the community is small and tight-knit.

problems.title: Only 28% Repeat Rate — Needlepointers Are Lifetime Buyers If Nurtured
problems.description: Needlepoint is inherently a repeat-purchase hobby. Once someone finishes a project, they want the next one. Art Needlepoint's 28% repeat rate is far below what a niche craft store should achieve. The 'Buy 3 Get 1 Free' promo exists but isn't triggered at the right post-purchase moment. No automated sequence introduces the next project when the current one is likely being finished (4–12 weeks after purchase depending on kit size).
problems.impact: Improving repeat rate from 28% to 45% on 320 monthly orders at $85 AOV = $4,624/month in additional revenue from existing customers — zero ad spend.
problems.evidence: Craft industry repeat purchase benchmarks: 40–55% for specialty retailers with active post-purchase engagement. Art Needlepoint's family-owned warmth is a retention advantage that isn't being systematized.

problems.title: 22% Open Rate on 12K List — 'Mondays with Needlepoint' Isn't Personalized
problems.description: Art Needlepoint has a 12,000-subscriber email list — a massive asset for a niche ecommerce store. But 22% open rate means 78% aren't engaging. 'Mondays with Needlepoint' is one-size-fits-all: a beginner gets the same email as a 20-year veteran. No segmentation by skill level, purchase history, or project interest. A customer who just bought a Christmas stocking kit should get finishing tips and ornament kit suggestions — not a generic newsletter.
problems.impact: Improving open rate from 22% to 35% and adding purchase-triggered sequences could drive $3,200+/month in additional email revenue.
problems.evidence: Mailchimp: retail email average open rate is 18.4%. Personalized product recommendation emails have 29% higher open rates and 41% higher click rates than generic sends.

problems.title: 180 Monthly Support Tickets — Skill-Level Questions Clog the Queue
problems.description: Art Needlepoint promises 'get a real person right away' — a beautiful differentiator. But 180 support tickets/month means Doreen and team are spending hours answering the same skill-level, thread, and shipping questions repeatedly. 60%+ of these are pre-purchase questions that could be answered by an AI assistant: 'Is this kit good for beginners?', 'What thread comes with this?', 'How long does this project take?' Freeing up Doreen for high-value customer relationships and product curation is the real win.
problems.impact: Automating 60% of routine inquiries saves 15–20 hours/month of staff time. Faster response to remaining tickets improves conversion on pre-purchase questions.
problems.evidence: Gorgias ecommerce benchmark: 40–60% of customer support tickets are repetitive and automatable. Response time under 1 hour increases purchase probability by 7x.

systems.name: Positive Review Collector Agent
systems.problem_it_solves: Only 47 Google reviews despite thousands of happy customers — no system captures reviews at the peak satisfaction moment
what_it_does: Triggers review request at the perfect moment: 2–4 weeks after delivery (when the customer has started stitching and is excited)
Pre-screens satisfaction with a simple 'How are you enjoying your kit?' message before sending the review link
Routes happy customers (8+/10) to Google review with a one-tap link and warm personal message
Routes unhappy customers (<8/10) to Doreen's support inbox — never to a public review page
Requests photo reviews specifically — 'Share a photo of your project in progress!' for the Customer Gallery
Sends a second review request at project completion (6–12 weeks) for transformation-style reviews with finished photos
Tracks review velocity and star rating trend vs. competitors weekly

personalization.brand_tone: Warm, personal, family-owned craft business. Doreen's personality shines through — approachable, passionate about needlepoint, treats every customer like a fellow stitcher. Never corporate, always human.
personalization.messaging_style: Lead with the review collector and sentiment analysis — Doreen is EXCITED about this. Show how it protects the brand while systematically building trust. Then show the full ecommerce flywheel: reviews → trust → conversion → retention → more reviews.
personalization.hook_question: If you could capture a Google review from every happy customer — and make sure unhappy customers never hit the review page — what would that do for your business?
personalization.demo_angle: Open with the Positive Review Collector: 'You have thousands of happy customers who spent 40–200 hours on a project and felt genuine joy when they finished. That emotion is the most powerful marketing asset you have — and right now it's not being captured.' Show the sentiment analysis: screen satisfaction BEFORE asking for reviews. Then expand: cart recovery, post-purchase nurture, email personalization. Close with the math: recovering 10% of abandoned carts + improving repeat rate from 28% to 45% = $10K+/month in new revenue from customers you already have.
personalization.value_proposition: Turn every happy stitcher into a public advocate, protect the brand from negative reviews, and build a repeat-purchase engine that turns one-time buyers into lifetime needlepoint customers — automatically.
personalization.the_personal_angle: Art Needlepoint is a family business built on love for the craft. The AI isn't replacing Doreen's personal touch — it's ensuring that personal touch reaches every customer, not just the ones who happen to call. The sentiment analysis protects what Doreen has built.

closer_note.headline: How to Run This Demo — Closer's Playbook
steps: 1. OPEN with the hook question: 'Doreen, you have thousands of happy customers who spent 40–200 hours on a project and felt real joy when they finished. Are you capturing that emotion as a Google review?' Let her answer. She will say no.

2. GO TO Profile → Recommended Systems → Positive Review Collector (the flagship ⭐ system). Walk through the sentiment-gating flow: satisfaction check FIRST, then route happy customers to Google and unhappy ones privately to Doreen's inbox. This is her #1 pain — lean into it.
3. SHOW the Sentiment Analysis Engine immediately after — explain it's the intelligence layer behind the review collector. It's what ensures no bad review ever slips through accidentally.
4. TRANSITION naturally: 'Now that we've protected your brand and started building reviews — let's look at the revenue you're losing every single day on the sales side.'
5. GO TO Problems tab → lead with ABANDONED CARTS (68%). Show the $5.7K/month number. Ask: 'Do you have any automated follow-up running right now when someone abandons?' She doesn't.
6. GO BACK TO Profile → Cart Recovery Agent. Walk the 3-touch sequence: 1hr / 24hr / 72hr with the real example output. Mention the Buy 3 Get 1 Free trigger built into the recovery email.
7. SHOW Post-Purchase Nurture Agent next — the 8–12 week project timer that fires when the kit should be done. This is the repeat rate play: 28% → 45%.
8. CLOSE with the pitch math: Cart recovery ($5.7K) + repeat rate lift ($4.6K) + email improvement ($3.2K) = $13K+/month in new revenue from customers she already has. Zero new ad spend.

9. HANDLE OBJECTION ('I'm a small business'): 'That's exactly why this works — you already have the customers and the goodwill. The AI just makes sure every one of them gets the follow-up they deserve, not just the ones who happen to call.'
10. ASK for the close: 'Would it make sense to start with the Review Collector and Cart Recovery — those two alone pay for the whole system in the first month?'
